setting: An international student picks up updated immigration documents at the international student office before traveling home.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and an advisor at the international student office.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Hi. I'm here to pick up my updated I-20. I travel home next week for the break.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Sure. May I see your student ID and passport? I also need you to sign the travel endorsement page.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Here they are. Do I need a new visa stamp, or is this enough?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: If your visa stamp is still valid, you only need the travel signature on the I-20. Yours looks valid through next August.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: I'll be gone three weeks. Should I report my travel dates in the portal?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Yes—enter your departure and return dates before you leave. If your return flight changes, update it within five days of landing.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Can I work on campus during the break if I come back early?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: On-campus work is fine during the official break as long as you remain enrolled for next term. Off-campus work still needs separate authorization.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Understood. Is there anything else I should carry at the airport?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Carry your passport, I-20, and proof of enrollment—an unofficial transcript printout works. Keep digital copies too, but officers usually want paper.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Great. I'll sign and update the portal tonight.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What is the conversation mainly about?

options.text: Picking up travel documents and rules before a trip home
Applying for a campus parking permit
Changing the student's major before graduation

questions.explanation: He picks up an updated I-20 and learns travel reporting and what to carry.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A—academics are not the topic.
questions.correctAnswer: Picking up travel documents and rules before a trip home

questions.narrator_text: What does he need if his visa stamp is still valid?

options.text: Only the travel signature on the I-20

questions.explanation: With a valid visa stamp, he only needs the travel signature on the I-20.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A—she says a new stamp is not required if the current one is valid.
questions.correctAnswer: Only the travel signature on the I-20

questions.narrator_text: What must he do about travel dates in the portal?

options.text: Delete his enrollment record while traveling
Only report dates after he comes back
Enter departure and return dates before leaving, and update within five days if the return flight changes

questions.explanation: Enter dates before departure; update within five days of landing if the return flight changes.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing B—he must enter dates before leaving, not only after return.
questions.correctAnswer: Enter departure and return dates before leaving, and update within five days if the return flight changes

questions.narrator_text: What should he carry at the airport?

options.text: Only a digital photo of his student ID
Passport, I-20, and proof of enrollment on paper, plus digital copies
His dorm room key and laundry card
Cash for a new visa stamp on arrival

questions.explanation: Passport, I-20, and paper proof of enrollment; digital copies are backup.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A—officers usually want paper documents.
questions.correctAnswer: Passport, I-20, and proof of enrollment on paper, plus digital copies
